## re-running samples 

Always good to check your outputs. 

In the `trimmomatic` step of our pipeline, we use our `catcher` function to see whether all samples were processed, and it suggests (because it should return missing samples) that everything went fine (i.e. it does not return any sample IDs.)
  
```{bash catch_trimms}
# again, using the catcher function we wrote in the programme-set up stage. 
catcher $filt 

# looks okay, but...
```
 
**However**, __if we check the `slrm` log outputs__ from the `trimmomatic` step, we will see a different story:


  
```{bash grep_trimms}
# again, using the catcher function we wrote in the programme-set up stage. 
grep "rror" ./omm__2* 
```

```
>  ./omm__2__trimmo4.1228821.slrm:slurmstepd: error: *** JOB 1228821 ON adacompute01 CANCELLED AT 2026-06-16T17:09:21 DUE TO TIME LIMIT ***
>  ./omm__2__trimmo4.1228846.slrm:slurmstepd: error: *** JOB 1228846 ON adacompute01 CANCELLED AT 2026-06-16T17:36:51 DUE TO TIME LIMIT ***
>  ./omm__2__trimmo4.1228851.slrm:slurmstepd: error: *** JOB 1228851 ON adacompute01 CANCELLED AT 2026-06-16T17:39:51 DUE TO TIME LIMIT ***
>  ./omm__2__trimmo4.1228853.slrm:slurmstepd: error: *** JOB 1228853 ON adacompute01 CANCELLED AT 2026-06-16T17:43:21 DUE TO TIME LIMIT ***
```
We have a problem - 4 samples (note that the IDs are not mentioned) took took longer than we defined in our `slurm` script, so the `HPC` killed those processes. However, because `trimmomatic` was running, some files _were_ produced, and these were picked up by `catcher`, which is why it looked like everything was fine. We can assume that these four files are broken, malformed, incomplete - or all of the above. 

With Kraken2, we can see a similar thing (presumably due to server overloading):

```
Loading database information...slurmstepd: error: *** JOB 1230249 ON adacompute01 CANCELLED AT 2026-06-23T12:12:04 DUE TO TIME LIMIT ***
```

<br>

So wat do. We need to get those ID's, increase the time limit on trimmomatic, and re-submit those 4 sample to `SLURM`. We could also consider deleting the incomplete outputs, just to be safe. 

You can do this manually if you like (it would take about three minutes) but for funs' sake we're going to script it here (an hour to code, +1 second to run). 


```{bash get_bad_trimm__UNFINISHED}
# -L option just returns the logfile - we grab the id from that.
grep -l "rror" ./omm__2*
# 

# add that grep into a for-loop and search for samople IDs:
for slrm in $( grep -l "rror" ./omm__2* ) ;
do
  grep -E ".*__join\/.*_R1.*" $slrm ;
done


##  no fgood solve yet :(
# # challenge: output is long, with multiple instances of that ID. how to parse properly?
# for slrm in $( grep -l "rror" ./omm__2* ) ;
# do
# grep -E ".*__join\/.*_R1.*" $slrm | sed -E 's/.*__join\/(.*)_R1.*/########\1#######/g' ;
# done

```


Copy and paste and write it down. No shame.

```
vaginal-69-Visit-1_S36
vaginal-95-Visit-1_S45
vaginal-98-Visit-3_S96
vaginal-9-Visit-3_S56

```

First, inspect and then delete the broken versions:

```{bash check_files }
# always inspect before deleting something - just to be sure.
lk $filt/{vaginal-69-Visit-1_S36,vaginal-95-Visit-1_S45,vaginal-98-Visit-3_S96,vaginal-9-Visit-3_S56}*

# Note: the $filt/{a,b,c,d}* format used finds any file matching that format. (a bash trick called globbing)

# if youre sure, delete them!
rm $filt/{vaginal-69-Visit-1_S36,vaginal-95-Visit-1_S45,vaginal-98-Visit-3_S96,vaginal-9-Visit-3_S56}*
```

then increase the max time limit on the `trimmo4.sh` script
```{bash nano_trimm}
nano $mat/ucc__fbio__slurm__trimmo4.sh    # from 20 to 30?
```


then refire with `SLURM`:

```{bash trimm_refire}
for id in vaginal-69-Visit-1_S36 vaginal-95-Visit-1_S45 vaginal-98-Visit-3_S96 vaginal-9-Visit-3_S56 ; 
do 
  sbatch $mat/${proj}__slurm__trimmo4.sh $id $join $filt ; 
done

```

Seems to work fine...

## `Kraken2` issues - erorr code 137

Computers give different "exit codes" based on the outcomes of a programme. If it succeeds and all is well, the standard exit code is `0`. Anything other than `0` means that something went wrong - but what?! 

<br> 

Solution one is learn an infinite number of non standard exit codes. Solution two is look up your exit code and apply its meanging to your workflow - what is it trying to say? `Kraken2` run at scale across the HPC can give the following exception:

```
# + + +   Kraken2 on vaginal-95-Visit-1_S45 -  conf 0.1, min-hits 5, min-qual 20; Bracken read:100, count:50
# Loading database information.../cm/local/apps/slurm/var/spool/job1230409/slurm_script: line 37: 444176 Killed                  kraken2 --db $kr_db $inpath/${samp}_R1_deco.fastq.gz $inpath/${samp}_R2_deco.fastq.gz --paired --threads $kr_threads --confidence 0.1 --gzip-compressed --report-zero-counts --minimum-hit-groups 5 --minimum-base-quality 20 --report $outpat/${samp}_kraken2_report --unclassified-out $outpat/${samp}_kraken_unclass# --output $outpat/${samp}_kraken_output
# < ! >    sample vaginal-95-Visit-1_S45 failed Kraken2 :: 137
```

A quick web search links `137` to `out of memory (OOM)` errors - `SLURM` is probably trying to load too many instances of the database into memory, and so is quickly running out of resources to do anythingand kills our job to avoid disaster. `SLURM` is literally designed for this situation, so it's nice that we didn't crash the aircraft - but how do we fix it?

 - consider [memory mapping](https://w3.cs.jmu.edu/kirkpams/OpenCSF/Books/csf/html/MMap.html). too tired ot read through as its actually about C# but idea holds
 
 - consider cp /tmp/shm

Hints from the underhive of `kraken2` issues:

  - https://github.com/DerrickWood/kraken2/issues/719 - deeper dive on `--mm` options, with subsequent [blogpost](https://avilpage.com/2024/07/mastering-kraken2-performance-optimisation.html). this points us towards `vmtouch`, which a little `grep -r` shows is waht we used with OMM: `cp -r $lang/*k2d /dev/shm/ ; vmtouch -t /dev/shm/*.k2d`
  -
